To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in any adapted atlas of the space–time, the field equations are solved with the help of one‐parameter groups generated by scalar and tensor Hamiltonians, that the Hilbert spaces of solutions of field equations are constructed and the corresponding canonical structures are determined, and that quantum field operators are defined, leading to the commutator of quantum field operators.

in static space–time, for the massive vector field, the Hilbert space of positive energy solutions, as well as that of negative energy solutions, is determined by the one‐particle Hilbert space, and that the Hilbert space for the quantum field is the Fock space of this one‐particle space.

the Hilbert space of positive energy solutions, as well as the Hilbert space and the symplectic structure of reduced solutions, of the massive vector field equations, are independent of the adapted atlas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of a quantum theory in curved space–time for massive vector fields.
a generalization of the theory of the positive and negative frequency solution spaces for the Klein–Gordon equation in Minkowski space, to the massive vector field equations, in static space–time.
a new method of solution of field equations in space–time, based on a new concept of space–time, which is a generalization of the concept of Riemannian manifold.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the quantum field theory of the physical field of mass m and spin 1 in the space–time Vn×R is completely determined by the classical field equations and the postulated commutation relations for the quantum field operators.
the quantum field theory for this physical field in these space–time manifolds is well defined and is free from the problems of the usual quantum field theory.
the field equations for the massive vector field are solved in the space–times under consideration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have constructed the quantum theory of the massive vector field of spin 0 in any static space–times, and that the quantum theory is consistent.
the positive energy solutions of the field equations are the solutions of the Hamiltonians i−1T1−1 and the negative energy solutions those of i−1T0−1, the latter being the reduced solutions.

we have shown that the physical field equations for spin 1 and m≳0 are solvable by the one‐ parameter groups of unitary transformations in Sobolev space, and that the quantum field operators for the physical fields are well defined.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the field equations are solved by the same one‐parameter group of unitary operators in the same Hilbert spaces, independently of the choice of the space–time atlas.
the construction of the Hilbert spaces of frequency solutions of field equation, as well as the construction of the corresponding quantum field operators, can be done in a unified manner.
the Hilbert spaces of solutions of field equations are determined by the geometry of space–time and the physical nature of the field.
